name: vray-6
label: V-Ray 6 (3ds Max)

maps.notes: Bitmap gamma Override 1.0: the file is already sRGB-encoded, and letting Max apply its default 2.2 a second time is the classic washed-out V-Ray material.
Green +Y (OpenGL) in Max; verify per host, since the same material in SketchUp or Rhino can be the other convention. 16-bit prevents banding on large flat surfaces.
Gamma 1.0. Modern V-Ray takes roughness directly; the legacy Glossiness input wants a curve, not a plain inversion, and this preset does not ship that curve.
2D displacement, amount in mm, mid-level 0.5. TIFF rather than the schema example's EXR because this build writes PNG and TIFF; the sample depth is the same 16 bits.
Use as a mask: V-Ray has its own ambient occlusion, and adding a baked one on top doubles it.
sRGB. The HDR multiplier belongs on the material, not in an 8-bit file.

notes: Use VRayTriplanar on curved or inconsistently UV'd geometry. This one note prevents the most visible class of wall artefacts.
Set Bitmap gamma to Override 1.0 on every data map -- roughness, metallic, height, normal. Only the albedo should be read as colour.
VRayDisplacementMod: 2D, amount 3.0 mm, midlevel 0.5. Raise the amount against the tile's real size if the mortar should read deeper.
VRayMultiSubTex can pack several of these into one bitmap to cut VRAM; if you do it, the maps stop being individually editable.
Written for V-Ray 5/6/7 on 3ds Max. The same files work in the SketchUp, Rhino and Blender integrations, where the slot names differ but the colour spaces do not.
IOR by material: 1.52 for most dielectrics, 1.55-1.6 for polished marble and granite, 1.76 for glass.
